title: Total left derivation sends an object short exact sequence to a distinguished triangle
statement:
Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B$ be abelian categories [def-sp-abelian]. Suppose $\mathcal A$ has enough projectives: every object is a quotient of an object $P$ such that maps from $P$ lift across epimorphisms. Let $V:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ be additive and right exact, meaning that it preserves cokernels and finite direct sums. Write $K(\mathcal A)$ and $K(\mathcal B)$ for the homotopy categories of integer cochain complexes and $Q_{\mathcal A},Q_{\mathcal B}$ for their localizations at quasi-isomorphisms [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Assume the total left derived functor $LV:D(\mathcal A)\to D(\mathcal B)$ of the termwise functor $Q_{\mathcal B}K(V)$ is defined at every object in the essentially-constant denominator-diagram sense [def-pur-saturated-triangulated-localization], with canonical natural comparison $\varepsilon_C:LV(Q_{\mathcal A}C)\to Q_{\mathcal B}V(C)$. Write $M[0]$ for the complex concentrated in degree zero. For a short exact sequence $0\to M'\xrightarrow{i}M\xrightarrow{p}M''\to0$, let $\delta:Q_{\mathcal A}(M''[0])\to Q_{\mathcal A}(M'[0])[1]$ be its canonical connecting morphism in $D(\mathcal A)$. Then $LV$ has its canonical exact triangulated structure, and the following triangle is distinguished in $D(\mathcal B)$:
$$LV(Q_{\mathcal A}(M'[0]))\xrightarrow{LV(Q_{\mathcal A}(i[0]))}LV(Q_{\mathcal A}(M[0]))\xrightarrow{LV(Q_{\mathcal A}(p[0]))}LV(Q_{\mathcal A}(M''[0]))\xrightarrow{\sigma_{M'}\circ LV(\delta)}LV(Q_{\mathcal A}(M'[0]))[1],$$
where $\sigma_{M'}:LV(Q_{\mathcal A}(M'[0])[1])\xrightarrow{\sim}LV(Q_{\mathcal A}(M'[0]))[1]$ is its shift comparison. No acyclicity of $M',M,M''$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 015D (lemma-F-acyclic-ses), proof, dualized: distinguished triangle construction and exactness of total left derivation (old Steps 2--3); supporting lemma-additive-exact-homotopy-category, lemma-acyclic, lemma-derived-canonical-delta-functor and proposition-derived-functor.

proof.text: Set $F=Q_{\mathcal B}\circ K(V)$. By [lem-trf-additive-homotopy-triangulated], additivity of $V$ makes $K(V)$ exact, including its canonical shift comparisons. By [lem-pur-quasi-isos-saturated-triangulated], applied to $\mathcal B$, $Q_{\mathcal B}$ is exact; the composite $F$ is therefore exact. The same node applied to $\mathcal A$ gives the saturated triangulated multiplicative system $S$ of quasi-isomorphisms required for left derivation.

The assumed total-derived pair $(LV,\varepsilon)$ has the right Kan universal property along $Q_{\mathcal A}$. Indeed, Step 1 makes $S$ a right multiplicative system with localization $Q_{\mathcal A}$, so [lem-pur-left-derived-defined-pointwise-kan-bridge] applies at every complex $X$ to the essentially constant denominator diagram: $F$ has a pointwise right Kan extension at $Q_{\mathcal A}X$ with value $LV(Q_{\mathcal A}X)$, by a limit cone whose leg at $(X',Q_{\mathcal A}(s)^{-1})$ is the essential-value leg $u_s=\varepsilon_{X'}\circ LV(Q_{\mathcal A}s)^{-1}$ and whose leg at $(X,\mathrm{id})$ is $\varepsilon_X$. The cone induced by $(LV,\varepsilon)$ at $Q_{\mathcal A}X$, with leg $\varepsilon_{X'}\circ LV(\varphi)$ at $(X',\varphi)$, has the same legs at these inverse-denominator objects; since every structured arrow receives a map from such an object (the representing right fraction), naturality makes the two cones equal, so the cone of $(LV,\varepsilon)$ is a limit. Every object of $D(\mathcal A)$ is isomorphic to some $Q_{\mathcal A}X$, and pointwise Kan extensions at all objects form a right Kan extension.

source.place: Tag 05S9 (definition-right-derived-functor-defined) and Tag 05SA (lemma-derived-functor), left derived parts

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-left-derived-exact-chosen-localization] with source $\mathcal A$, target $D(\mathcal B)$, the exact functor $F$ of Step 1 and the pair $(LV,\varepsilon)$ of Step 2. Its two existence hypotheses hold: the Kan property by Step 2, and essential constancy of the denominator diagrams at every complex by the item's hypothesis. It follows that $LV$ is exact with a shift structure for which $\varepsilon$ commutes with shifts. Its compatible shift is the canonical one: [lem-pur-right-kan-extension-coherent-shift] constructs the coherent comparisons from this same universal pair. Any two comparisons $c,c':LV\circ[n]\cong[n]\circ LV$ satisfying the counit square coincide. Write functors as acting right to left, so $GQ_{\mathcal A}$ means $Q_{\mathcal A}$ followed by $G$. For $G:D(\mathcal A)\to D(\mathcal B)$, the shift $[n]$ of $D(\mathcal B)$ being an equivalence with inverse $[-n]$, the universal property gives bijections $\mathrm{Nat}(G,[n]LV)\cong\mathrm{Nat}([-n]G,LV)\cong\mathrm{Nat}([-n]GQ_{\mathcal A},F)\cong\mathrm{Nat}(GQ_{\mathcal A},[n]F)$, the composite being whiskering by $Q_{\mathcal A}$ followed by composition with $[n]\varepsilon$. Take $G=LV[n]$: the counit square says that $c$ and $c'$ have the same image, namely the composite of the shift comparisons of $Q_{\mathcal A}$ and $F$ with $\varepsilon[n]$, so $c=c'$. In degree one denote this comparison by $\sigma_X:LV(X[1])\xrightarrow{\sim}LV(X)[1]$.

Apply [lem-sf-derived-ses-triangle] to the given short exact sequence in $\mathcal A$. This supplies the distinguished triangle with objects $Q_{\mathcal A}(M'[0])$, $Q_{\mathcal A}(M[0])$, $Q_{\mathcal A}(M''[0])$, first two arrows $Q_{\mathcal A}(i[0])$, $Q_{\mathcal A}(p[0])$, and canonical last arrow $\delta$. Here the canonical choice is the single-complex triangle, not an arbitrary completion of its first arrow.

source.place: Tag 0152 (lemma-derived-canonical-delta-functor); Tag 015D (lemma-F-acyclic-ses), first sentence of proof

proof.text: Apply the exact functor $LV$ from Step 3 to the distinguished triangle of Step 4. By the definition of exactness in [def-weil-triangulated-category], its last arrow is $LV(\delta)$ followed by $\sigma_{Q_{\mathcal A}(M'[0])}$. Its first two arrows are the images of $Q_{\mathcal A}(i[0])$ and $Q_{\mathcal A}(p[0])$. These are exactly the four arrows and three objects displayed in the statement. No comparison $\varepsilon$ is required to be invertible on these objects, so no acyclicity assumption enters.
